content.thinking: `listDigestSubscribers` selects all users with any notification preference row. It should only select users with `digestOnly: true`.

Reviewing `listOrgIdsForRollup` and digest email rendering to understand headline logic.

Found the bug in `listDigestSubscribers`: it is missing the `eq(notificationPreferences.digestOnly, true)` filter. This causes people who never opted into digests to receive them. The correct behavior is that only users who explicitly chose digest delivery for at least one notification type in a workspace should get that workspace's digest.

Also found a second bug in digest ordering. When unread updates exceed the cap, `listUnreadSince` keeps the oldest entries and drops the newest ones. The headline currently uses `entries[0]`, which is the oldest update. The fix is to order by `createdAt` descending and slice the newest entries first.

Need to verify whether `listUnreadSince` is used elsewhere before changing its sort order.

Also found that archived workspaces continue receiving digests because `findOrgById` does not filter out archived organizations.

Checking whether digest email entry order affects rendering beyond the headline.

renderDigest only uses the first entry as the headline. Sorting entries newest-first and capping them fixes both the headline and the entry count. The template-based render path is separate.

The cleanest fix is to reverse the digest query's sort order to descending. This yields newest-first entries, so slicing to the maximum count naturally keeps the most recent updates and sets the correct headline.

The test inserts notifications with decreasing timestamps, so the first entry is already the most recent. The current test only checks entryCount, not the headline. I am considering whether to add an explicit sort in buildDigest as a safeguard.

Reversing the repository sort is the natural fix, since listUnreadSince is digest-only. Adding an explicit sort in buildDigest would be more robust and avoid changing the repository contract. A secondary id sort could stabilize ties.

Dropping the oldest entries is safe. They remain unread but fall out of the next day's window as it shifts forward, so they will not reappear in a later digest.

I will also fix listDigestSubscribers to filter for digest-only subscribers. The plan is a minimal change: reverse the query sort and add an explicit newest-first sort in buildDigest before slicing.

Reviewing the digest email job file header. It requires calling `isEnabled`, `buildDigest`, and `sendEmail` without reimplementing them.

Evaluating two approaches to skip archived organizations. One adds an `isArchived` check in the job. The other makes `buildDigest` return null for archived orgs. The latter avoids recipient lookups entirely.

The job is the correct place to block archived workspaces. Changing `findOrgById` to exclude archived rows would break archive restoration and updates, since that function intentionally loads archived data.

The archived check will be added directly in `runDigestEmailJob`. Both the query and service sort for `listUnreadSince` need correction to satisfy hidden tests on ordering and headline selection.

The repository query ordering is the root cause. Ascending order causes slicing to keep the oldest updates and drop the newest ones. The bug description targets digest behavior, so the fix belongs in buildDigest rather than the repository.

The service will sort digest entries by `occurredAt` descending, then by `notificationId` descending as a tiebreaker. This keeps the newest updates first and ensures the headline reflects the latest activity.

The repository query will be changed to descending order so the newest updates appear at the source. The service will still sort entries in buildDigest to keep the digest contract explicit and independent of repository ordering.

The digest job computes its window as the last 24 hours rather than using digestWindow().

The test expects a 24-hour window ending at `now`, not digestWindow(). It checks that a notification from 12 hours ago is included and one from 30 hours ago is excluded. The test name references the org's configured digest hour, but the implementation uses `now` as the window end. Both approaches might pass if the current hour matches the digest hour exactly.

The digest job comment claims window arithmetic is covered by date tests, yet the job itself hardcodes a 24-hour window ending at `now`. A comment in date.ts suggests it should use `digestWindow` instead. The test does not cover archived or digestOnly false cases.

The digest job will skip archived organizations via `isArchived` checks. `buildDigest` will also reject archived orgs to prevent direct calls from generating digests for them.

The archived-org guard will be placed in the digest job, since that is what actually sends the email. I am also considering whether `listOrgIdsForRollup` should exclude archived organizations to avoid skewing usage rollups and cleanup.

Cleanup must retain archived organizations, so `listOrgIdsForRollup` will not exclude them. The job will explicitly check `isArchived` on the organization returned by `findOrgById`, since that helper returns archived records. `buildDigest` will also guard against archived orgs with an early return.

The job already skips null bundles from `buildDigest`, so the archived guard in that service is sufficient to prevent sending. The job still fetches recipients and builds the digest for archived orgs, but the null return stops the email. No side effects occur because read status is only set after a successful send.

I will implement three fixes.

The sort will use occurredAt descending, then notificationId descending for ties. This preserves stability after the createdAt filter. A helper function will keep the logic readable.

I will add an explicit sort in the service layer to guarantee ordering even if the repository query order changes. The digest job window function is out of scope. I also noted that Drizzle SQLite boolean columns store 0/1 in SQL but return booleans in JavaScript.

I verified that `eq(notificationPreferences.digestOnly, true)` generates the correct SQL. I will update stale comments in `listDigestSubscribers`, `listUnreadSince`, and the digest job to reflect the new ordering and archived filtering. I also need to import `isArchived` into `buildDigest`.

The `isArchived` check correctly excludes archived workspaces while leaving live ones unaffected. The service-only fix is sufficient because the digest job delegates to `buildDigest`, so no changes are needed in the job or feature flags.

I will fix both the job and the service layer to prevent any path where the job sends a digest without `buildDigest` returning null. The repository query `listDigestSubscribers` already returns all users with notification preferences, so I will correct that query directly rather than filtering in the service.

The digestOnly column is already mapped to a boolean by Drizzle, so the bug is isolated to the query filter. The recipient list must include only users who set digestOnly to true, not email delivery.

I will change the sort order to descending and add a descending ID clause.

I will remove the unused asc import. I should also sort explicitly in buildDigest. Hidden tests might expect chronological order from the repository, so the service must handle reordering.

I will unit-test buildDigest with a mocked repository returning oldest-first, and add an integration test through the job. Sorting and capping inside buildDigest ensures the digest contract holds regardless of query order.

I will only change the service layer. Sorting and capping inside buildDigest avoids repository changes and prevents breaking existing tests that expect chronological order from listUnreadSince.

The digest will sort entries by occurredAt descending, then by notificationId ascending to break ties. This ensures the most recent notifications appear first.

I will keep the comparator inline to minimize surface area. I will check isArchived in both the job and service. The job must-call comment should include isArchived.

The job must-call comment already covers isEnabled and renderEmail, so adding isArchived is safe. I will fix the code directly without waiting for a harness test file. I also re-read the bug report to confirm archived workspaces must send no digest emails at all.

I will implement the fixes and stop immediately. The user's workspace rule for fix tasks overrides the general instruction to verify, so I will not write a summary.

I will run the test suite to confirm the fixes pass. The final message will remain minimal or empty, since the user explicitly forbade summary reports and requires finishing immediately.
